rows: Anybody can swing twice. Knowing when not to swing is the lesson.
Brawling is easy to start. The hard part is knowing when to stop.
Nerve is a swing you cannot take back. Decide before you swing.
Slowing down is a lesson most people never learn. Learn it now.
The people paid for a contest, not a riot. Give them control.
Force without control is just noise, and I am not going to be noise.
I have taught this for a long time, and the lesson has not changed.
Look at the stance, then steady yourself. Balanced, not wild. That is the first thing to learn.
Technique, which you should use with restraint. Show me a hold you can release when the moment passes.
Strikes have their place. The place is not everywhere.
A gamble you cannot stop is not courage. It is a loss of control.
A stall is not restraint. It is hiding. I can tell the difference.
The people deserve a match that shows control. Give them the lesson.
You mock restraint. Watch what happens to the people who do not have it.
Proud of your {strength}, and holding it back? Good restraint. Now show me when you hold it back.
I have seen your {strength}, and it is strong. It is not yet controlled.
Composed, good. Good restraint. That is the first sign of control.
Noted. You have learned the first part of the lesson.
I could tell you what I think of that. I will tell you what you should do instead.
One fall, restraint. Keep me down with control, and I will say you did it properly.
On the mat, force does not win on its own. Control does.
Grounded or standing, the lesson holds. Control first.
Stay in front of me and show me the restraint.
That answer shows restraint. That is the right instinct.
Still no answer, and no hurry. Answer with control, not with volume.
Noted. That is a lesson worth keeping.
Understood. We will test the control at the bell.
I will wrestle this match with control, and I will finish it cleanly.
My approach is measured. You will see control on the night.
Whatever happens, I want you to leave knowing when to stop.
We are not done. There is still a lesson to finish.
I have one lesson left, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
I should have shown more restraint. I cannot give you evidence sufficient to establish the charge.
Control starts with knowing what not to say. I cannot substantiate that accusation, so it goes no further.
That is a controlled answer. Leave the accusation there and bring the same restraint to the ring.
Understood. The words need go no further. We can test our wrestling properly.
Watch which of us keeps control when the first move fails. That is the lesson the contest can demonstrate.
The people can judge how we use our strength, not just how much of it we have. Let the wrestling show them.
An accusation does not tell you whether someone has control. What can we demonstrate when we wrestle?
Save the judgement about the claim. What can the crowd learn from how we handle ourselves in the ring?
You've prepared to stop my {strength}. Do it with control, even when the first attempt doesn't go your way.
Knowing about my {strength} doesn't give you permission to lose your head when I use them. Keep your balance.
